To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a) we present the first deep learning method that can estimate 3D human poses from wide baseline views, b) we present the fist deep learning method that up-scales volumetric data by 4x, and c) we show that the proposed approach can be trained on synthetic data and applied on real images with no retraining.

(1) we propose a deep autoencoder that learns a joint representation of body shape and pose; (2) we use this representation to upscale input data by a factor 4x; (3) we show that our method outperforms the state-of-the-art on both pose and shape estimation tasks.
we propose a method for simultaneously recovering 3D human body shape and 3D human joint positions from wide-baseline camera images, using a symmetric deep autoencoder.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of estimating 3D body shape and pose from sparse camera views.

the following questions: (1) How to learn a joint representation of body pose and shape, (2) How to learn an up-scaling of volumetric body models and (3) How to use the learned up-scaling for human pose and shape estimation.
the development and evaluation of a deep learning method for human shape and pose estimation from a sparse set camera views, with a focus on up-scaling volumetric body data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our work demonstrates a novel approach for simultaneously estimating 2D and 3D human body shape and joint positions from wide-baseline camera data.
we present a method for estimating human body shape and joint positions from sparse wide-baseline views, and that it is the first to achieve this.

the proposed approach is able to estimate the 3D human body pose and shape in a real-time fashion from a sparse set (2-3) of wide-baseline cameras, and that it is able to upscale input volumetric data to the resolution of a full-body scan (4×) whilst simultaneously estimating 3-D human body pose.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel approach for human body shape and 3D pose estimation from a sparse set (3-4) of wide-baseline views.
our method can be used to up-scale volumetric data by 4× whilst recovering a 2.5D pose estimate of equal or higher accuracy compared to the state of the-art, and all this in real-time.

we have developed a deep learning based approach for simultaneous human pose and shape estimation from sparse views that outperforms the state-of-the-art in terms of accuracy, while running in real-time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
deep autoencoders are a powerful and flexible tool for joint estimation and upscaling of 3D human body data.
a single model can learn a deep representation of body shape, which can then be used to up-scale volumetric data, whilst simultaneously learning a deep latent representation of human pose.
the joint representation of pose and shape in a single latent space allows for a more efficient representation of the data and can be used for simultaneous estimation of both.
